I brought my k9 protection dog and my leopard gecko here due to rashes on my dog and an infection in my geckos eye. However when I arrived and was roomed my dog immediately started to get anxious, which is unlike him. He is usually very calm at the vet. The doctor ( Dr. Hitzschky)  came in and didn’t greet him or show him that he could trust her. To my dog and his training, that is very important. As soon as he saw her putting on the gloves he was barking nonstop, immediately no trust. He didn’t want to be near her either. He wouldn’t take treats from her and he positioned himself in a corner with me alert constantly. At some point she refused to give him an updated rabies vaccine without proof his previous one expired even though I’ve gone to many vets who give them without documentation. When I tried to decline the rabies shot (because we were there for allergies) she said that it’s office policy that they must have their rabies vaccine in the office, almost saying that I couldn’t leave unless he had an updated vaccine. I was not informed that beforehand.  My dog picked up on her condesending attitude as his job is to observe body language. This is the type of doctor who thinks she’s an animal person but yet knows hardly anything about them. She interrupts, makes you feel dumb and is just plain rude. I can bet half of her staff probably don’t like her. At one point they wanted to seperate us because he wouldn’t stop barking, and he continued to bark in the back and would not let them touch him, so I was told. The doctor suggested a
“ muzzle” even though he wouldn’t bite unless told. She told me to come back after he’s taken some anti ANXIETY medication, which they prescribed and he has yet to take. Then charged me over $260…. To do literally NOTHING.  The vet tech was alright, she was sweet. My gecko wasn’t handled the most gently by this doctor, hence why she defecated and bit her. My gecko has never bit me!!!! Now they want me to come back and pay $123 more just to give an injection I already paid for. I suggest going somewhere else who doesn’t charge $123 for an office visit and knows how to handle k9 dogs and reptiles. ( AND BIRDS.)

UPDATE: I ended up going to a new vet and had zero issues with them as they gave him his updated vaccines and treated his allergies.
And I’ll be going to a professional for my gecko.

WARNING TO QUAIL AND SMALL BIRD OWNERS: please never take your beloved bird here and heed the reviews from other bird owners. We took one of our quail here a few years ago (July 2021) and she was handled so roughly that one of her legs was permanently crippled. The “doctor” and “nurse” literally pulled her leg and twisted the joint in a split second, and her claws were clipped so short that they bled. It was so shocking. We will never forget her expression as she winced in unbearable pain and hobbled over on the treatment table, never to walk normally again.

The “doctor” and “nurse” tried to gaslight us, claiming that her joint was already twisted even though our quail had walked normally for THREE YEARS before we took her to this horrid place. They completely avoided responsibility for their actions, saying they’d throw in a few minutes in the cold chamber for free as part of her treatment, as if that was supposed to do anything or mean anything. RIDICULOUS!!

We were so sad and in shock that we didn’t even leave a review, but it is so cruel and disheartening that she had to live the last year of her life in pain due to the unethical negligence of the doctor and nurse at the time. On the anniversary of her passing, we are leaving this review in honor of her strength and for other bird owners. It is what she would have wanted.

Given some of the other reviews by bird owners, including domestic species, it is ridiculous and  unethical that this place advertises itself as an “avian” clinic. Birds are FRAGILE and should be handled with just as much care as other species. If not, it is misleading to advertise as an avian clinic.

My leopard gecko had been having issues for a few months with shedding and built up a crusty patch on both eyes. I had tried reaching out to multiple exotic pet vets in the area but everyone would get back with me saying they don’t do lizards. I’m so glad I found this clinic! We had two appointments with Dr Wilson and she was so gentle and kind. I felt like a terrible pet parent bc I had let our gecko get to the point she had gotten but I never felt judged by Dr Wilson or the staff. She was able to remove the built up shed and prescribed eye drops, oral antibiotics for another issue, and some NSAIDs for any related discomfort. They also provided guidance on how to administer everything and an info sheet on proper care. Although I felt like we knew how to care for our gecko and had the proper setup, it turns out we were missing some key parts of her care. Her habitat is setup properly now. She lost quite a bit of weight over the last several months and wasn’t eating, likely due to both her inability to see from the shed buildup, the infection, and the discomfort. We weren’t sure if she would be able to see even after removing the shed and treating the infection, and I’ve been worried about her not eating but today I woke up to her outside of her hide looking very lively and watching me walk around again for the first time in many months. I refilled her bowl and she seemed really interested and hungry so I tried to feed her with tongs and she ate 12 worms for the first time in probably 6-8 months!! She seems like she is finally feeling like her old self again and can see. I’m so grateful for Dr Wilson, the staff, and the clinic.

Re:pricing - this is part of the reason I put this off so long. In addition to most clinics stating they don’t help reptiles, I was afraid I would be spending 1000s of dollars on diagnostics. They provide an estimate up front of the anticipated diagnostics, medications, and services and then my actual cost ended up being less than the estimate. I like that they do this, it’s the opposite of sticker shock. They prepare you for worst case scenario with the cost and then don’t end up having to do everything they might have needed to do for worst case scenario so the cost is less. I really appreciate this. The pricing either way was a lot less than I expected.

I had a terrible experience with Summertree. I tried them because of their excellent reviews. I brought my 7mo old kittens in for a check-up and behavior consult. It was my kittens 1st visit to SUmmerTree. Dr. Joiner saw them both at 8 AM on Saturday. By 9 PM Sunday night, my little girl had died from Feline Infectious Peritonitis at the Vet ER. The ER sent the report to Summertree, but they did not call me back on Monday. Neither did I hear from them on Tuesday so I called them and asked to speak with the doctor. She called back. She expressed her condolences on the phone and in an email. But that was it. I asked how it could be that a kitten was brought to them for care on one day, and on the next day that kitten is gone. I didn't get anything resembling an answer or any admission of guilt. Now imagine if this were a human baby.  It is very hard for me to understand how a medical professional can miss glaring problems and still be considered a professional. Note too: Summertree made no gesture to refund any of the expenses I incurred there.  They seem like very nice people. I wish i could tender a better report, but my experience was traumatic.

(Now I hope they do not reply here, as that would add insult to injury; any reply here would simply be a vain attempt at damage control.)

We brought our parakeet, Peaches, to Dr. Nasser. She told us Peaches had been egg bound meaning she couldn't pass her eggs due to their soft shell. Instead of recognizing it was a medical emergency, she insisted we buy $27 meloxicam to help her pass the eggs and to bring her back almost 4 days later for a "high risk removal" if she had not passed them. Even though  during the examination Peaches had stopped breathing twice and instead of trying to save her, she asked if CPR should be preformed instead of acting on it- as if that should even be a question?! However, being unaware of the importance of time in this situation, and her insistance that Peaches could die if she tried to remove her eggs herself (as a physician with years of schooling trained for situations like this, mind you, but I digress) we listened and brought her back home. But she passed. Even after we texted the clinic informing the eggs had not been passed prior to Peaches death, they did nothing.
After researching, we realized that every avian vet should know how life threatening an eggbound egg is, especially to a small bird. Do not come here, the negligence they are getting away with is truly shocking.
